requirements.statement: A packet requires resolved decisions with alternatives, evidence, costs and acyclic dependencies
requirements.counterexample: A blocked decision, empty evidence or missing option cost can be locked

requirements.statement: A mutating graph requires a current locked packet and carries it into agent context
requirements.counterexample: A graph with no spec compiles or its emitted agents never receive requirement ids

requirements.statement: Declared check errors, timeouts, missing tools, unarmed formal escape-hatch ratchets and failed proof witnesses prevent success
requirements.counterexample: A failed check, unarmed proof ratchet or absent prover is silently treated as a pass

requirements.statement: Spec edits, named obligation drift and proof baseline changes invalidate the lock, parsed packet and digest share one byte snapshot, and recording rejects an absent or stale identity
requirements.counterexample: A weaker theorem or a packet parsed before replacement is stamped with the replacement identity

requirements.statement: Before the next check or final identity validation, terminate check descendants in the POSIX process group or Windows job, including on timeout and early parent exit
requirements.counterexample: A timed-out check leaves a child that writes into the checkout after the runner returns

requirements.statement: A WORK.md spec declaration arms the scaffolded harness and a mere Decisions mention cannot exempt statement drift
requirements.counterexample: Deleting a declared packet or mentioning an obligation leaves the gate green

requirements.statement: The token estimate, emitted cost metadata and compilation ceiling account for the injected packet on every agent call that receives it
requirements.counterexample: A large packet compiles below the declared cost ceiling because only graph orchestration was priced

requirements.statement: A RedTeamV1 BLOCK prevents a COMPLETE record even with empty findings and retains additional review evidence
requirements.counterexample: Missing coverage is reported as BLOCK with no invented vulnerability, but recording silently marks it COMPLETE

requirements.statement: Opt-in lanes execute concurrently with explicit joins, mutation branch exclusion, budget reservations and shared halt; replay keys bind exact prompts, options, launch and ancestors, with fresh sentinel readings and independent source journal/transcript verification
requirements.counterexample: A live ancestor, moved branch, ambiguous transcript or forged memo reuses a green result

requirements.statement: Embedded args retain exact note text, reject inline overrides and silent dropping, and resume assembly accepts only named changes while verifying full evidence-file SHA-256 pins
requirements.counterexample: An unchanged epoch drifts or a pinned evidence file changes without refusing launch

requirements.statement: A green gate cannot hide an earlier red at the same tree and launch; one manifest-pinned classified crash may be closed only by one clean native and one digest-pinned reference execution with retained reverified logs
requirements.counterexample: Assertion failure or an unpaired red is silently superseded by a later green

requirements.statement: CI-backed claims re-read forge heads, all relevant status/check rows, pinned witness identities and unchanged coverage inputs at record time; dirty local evidence cannot back a claim
requirements.counterexample: A self-authored green row, moved PR head or modified pipeline helper admits a pass

requirements.statement: Packet locks include inferred tracked test-support closure, planned locked edits refuse, reachability preflight reports affected checks, and a packet conflict can only block work
requirements.counterexample: An imported fixture changes outside the trust base or a conflict authorizes a weaker check

requirements.statement: Repair completion and checked-commit discharge require harness-defined patch SHA and added-hunk coverage, independent sibling attacks and structurally spawned attackers/refuters with no open blocking findings
requirements.counterexample: A narrow original-attack PASS or forged diff receipt marks unchecked repair commits as checked

challenges.claim: A complete-looking spec can still express the wrong requirement
challenges.resolution: The grill pass records counterexamples and challenges; independent verification and real runtime checks remain required

challenges.claim: An agent can rewrite both the packet and its lock
challenges.resolution: The lock is a drift boundary and a reviewable artifact; CI and review remain the external trust boundary

challenges.claim: A missing response could be mistaken for authorization
challenges.resolution: Defaulted decisions remain model recommendations; genuine authority boundaries remain blocked

challenges.claim: Installing a plugin might be mistaken for upgrading every consuming harness
challenges.resolution: New initialization requires integration; existing copied harnesses need an explicit update
